questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The quality that makes an animal glad to eat a feed because it tastes good to it, whether fresh and juicy or otherwise, is called
questions.explanation: The tongue decides before the stomach does.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: A young bull in the herd develops a hot swelling on the thigh, limps and dies quickly. The disease that causes such gassy muscle swellings in young cattle is
questions.explanation: The swelling crackles under the fingers.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: A poultry disease caused by bacteria in which adult hens grow pale, droop, lose appetite and their laying drops sharply is
questions.explanation: The pale comb tells of the fever within.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: A maize plant sends out extra shoots from its base near the soil, so that one stand later carries several stems. This production of side shoots is called
questions.explanation: One seed becomes a small family of stems.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The washing down of minerals and other materials from the upper layer of a soil into the layer beneath it is called
questions.explanation: The top layer gives; the layer below receives.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The reddish, iron-rich tropical soil, soft when dug from below but hardening like brick on exposure to sun and air, is
questions.explanation: Cut it and leave it; it soon sets like stone.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The club formed in many secondary schools, in which students keep a school garden and rear small animals to learn farming practically, is the
questions.explanation: Members learn farming with their own hands.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The World Bank-assisted Nigerian project under which farmers in the low, seasonally flooded valley bottoms of the north grow irrigated vegetables and rice is the
questions.explanation: Its name is the Hausa word for the wet lowlands.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The government authorities created in the 1970s to control rivers, build dams and provide water all year for irrigation farming in their areas are the
questions.explanation: Each watches over the rivers of its own basin.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The programme launched in 1980 by the Nigerian government, using fertiliser subsidies and new seeds to push the country towards growing enough food for itself, was the
questions.explanation: Its name promised fields of plenty.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The 1978 decree that vested all land in each state in the hands of the military governor, making farmers seek rights of occupancy, is the
questions.explanation: Land title now flowed from the governor's office.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The short, pointed, T-handled tool with which a farmer makes small holes in the seedbed and drops seeds into them one by one is the
questions.explanation: Poke, drop, cover: the hole-maker earns its name.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The one-wheeled cart with two handles, pushed like a barrow, with which a worker carries small loads of manure or harvest across the farm, is the
questions.explanation: One wheel, two handles, many trips.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: A hen lays one egg each day for about three weeks, then pauses and turns broody. The whole batch of eggs she lays before pausing is called a
questions.explanation: The eggs come in one unbroken run.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: A dairy farmer gives his in-calf cow a rising allowance of rich concentrate in the last weeks before calving, so that she calves strongly and milks well. This feeding is
questions.explanation: The udder is prepared before the calf arrives.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The warm cabinet in a poultry house, heated by electricity or kerosene, in which fertile eggs are turned daily until they hatch, is an
questions.explanation: The eggs rest in its steady warmth.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The price a farmer receives for his produce right at the farm, before any transporter or middleman adds his own cost, is the
questions.explanation: It is what the buyer pays at the gate.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The chain of traders — assemblers, wholesalers and retailers — who stand between the farmer and the final consumer of his produce are collectively called
questions.explanation: The produce passes through their hands.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The minimum price at which the government promises to buy a farmer's grain in a season of plenty, so that he is not ruined by crashing prices, is the
questions.explanation: The farmer can plant without fear of a crash.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: A tree crop of the savanna belt, grown in Kogi and Enugu for its curved, kidney-shaped nut and its juicy false fruit, is the
questions.explanation: The nut hangs below a swollen juicy apple.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The gum, tapped from thorny acacia trees of the Sudan savanna and exported for use in sweets and inks, is
questions.explanation: The bark is cut and the gum oozes out.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: After harvest, freshly dug yams are kept warm and shaded for some days until their small wounds dry and heal over before storage. This treatment is called
questions.explanation: Healed wounds refuse the rot entry.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Rice paddy is first soaked and steamed, then dried before milling, so that the grain hardens and keeps more of its food value. This treatment is
questions.explanation: The half-cooked grain resists breaking in the mill.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: On a poultry farm, eggs are examined and sorted by weight and shell quality before packing, the big ones apart from the small. This process is
questions.explanation: Each size travels to its own crate.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Fish in a crowded pond gasp at the surface at dawn because the level of the gas they need in the water has fallen. That gas is
questions.explanation: Their breath is dissolved in the water.
